what: Short test sentences for the ASR round-trip test (speak with the engine, transcribe, compare), one entry per voice tag in langs.tsv (155). Up to 8 sentences per tag. Common Voice is used first, Tatoeba fills gaps. Selection is deterministic: Common Voice files are read in the order sentence-collector.txt, then Wikipedia-extract files (wiki.*, *.wiki.*, hy_wiki.txt) alphabetically, using the first 400,000 bytes of each, and lines are taken in file order (files are sorted alphabetically); Tatoeba *_sentences_detailed.tsv.bz2 rows are taken in file (sentence id) order. A sentence qualifies if it has 4 to 15 whitespace-separated words (Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Burmese: 8 to 30 letters and no Latin letters) and contains no digits, no URLs, no brackets, no quotation marks (apostrophes are allowed), no ellipsis, none of / \ # % & * _ = + | ~ ^ $ EUR GBP section @ broken-bar multiplication-sign bullet middle-dot, no private-use characters (e.g. Tengwar), starts with a letter (an opening inverted question or exclamation mark is allowed), has no word mixing Latin, Cyrillic and Greek letters, and is not all capitals. It must also not start with a lower-case letter (except Lojban, written in lower case), and every letter must be in the main script of its file (the most common script among the letters of the Common Voice chunk or Tatoeba file), which drops stray English, Roman-Urdu and mixed-script lines. Punjabi lines that begin with the lone letter U+0A05 (a list-marker artefact) are skipped. Duplicates are dropped. A Common Voice line wholly wrapped in one pair of double quotes (a file-format artefact, as in pl) is unwrapped first. One Tatoeba row (9844546, an Urdu sentence filed as Sindhi) is excluded by id. Every Tatoeba sentence was checked with the Tatoeba API (api.tatoeba.org/v1/sentences/<id>) and kept only if its licence is CC BY 2.0 FR or CC0 1.0 and it is not marked unapproved. Common Voice is preferred when it gives at least 5 sentences. Accent and dialect tags reuse the parent tag's sentences. Europarl, Wikisource, Wikidata and other Common Voice files are not used; UDHR, FLORES and Wikipedia text are not used. Tatoeba sentences are CC BY 2.0 FR (attribution: sentence id and author, https://tatoeba.org/sentences/show/<id>) unless their "licence" says CC0 1.0. Built by a script outside the repository.
